intended_object: The property of a finite-type affine group scheme G over a field k being semisimple: G is smooth and geometrically connected and its geometric radical is trivial, i.e. every connected normal smooth solvable closed subgroup of G over the algebraic closure of k is trivial (Milne, Algebraic Groups §§6.46, 21.10). Inferred from the docstring, the name and the module documentation.
explanation: The definition pulls back the coordinate-ring predicate `semisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty k` along the inverse of the anti-equivalence between finite-type commutative Hopf algebras and finite-type affine group schemes. So G has the property exactly when its coordinate Hopf algebra does (`semisimpleAffineGroupSchemeProperty_iff` holds by `Iff.rfl`). Because the transport is along an equivalence, it preserves meaning and isomorphism invariance. The Hopf-side predicate unfolds to three conditions: Algebra.Smooth k H; geometric connectedness; and, for every normal Hopf ideal I of the base change H ⊗ k̄ whose quotient is geometrically connected, smooth and has a solvable group of algebraically-closed-field-valued points, I equals the augmentation ideal, which corresponds to the trivial subgroup. This is the standard definition: G is smooth and connected with trivial geometric radical, stated through the radical's universal property as the largest connected normal smooth solvable subgroup. Requiring smoothness of the candidate subgroups is correct, because in positive characteristic semisimple groups can have non-smooth connected central subgroup schemes. For smooth groups over an algebraically closed field, solvability of the group of points is equivalent to solvability as an algebraic group. The setting (finite-type affine group schemes over a field) is the natural one for this notion. Mathlib has no notion of semisimple algebraic group.
